correctness.rationale: Invariance against arbitrary antiderivatives of one-coordinate tests yields \(\mathbb E[xy^\gamma\mid x]=1\) and \(\mathbb E[xy^\gamma\mid y]=y\). The residuals are exactly \(-\dot x\) and \(\dot y/\alpha\), producing the variance identity by conditional orthogonality. Strict Jensen inequalities applied to \(y^{1-\gamma}\) and \(y^\gamma\), together with complete-trajectory classification of equality, give the arithmetic/reciprocal mean shifts and the two-sided crossing theorem. The packaged exact checker verifies the algebra independently.

value.rationale: The observable \(xy^\gamma\) is the defining nonlinear glycolytic reaction flux, so its two exact conditional calibrations are intrinsic to the model rather than arbitrary statistics. The theorem explains how the same flux can be mean-independent of substrate while being positively coupled to product, and converts the mismatch between those two regressions into exact dynamical activity. The strict arithmetic and reciprocal mean shifts force every non-equilibrium compact recurrent state to straddle both equilibrium concentration levels, yielding a direct qualitative diagnostic for periodic Selkov oscillations.
